overview: St Michael’s Mount is the little castle-topped island you’ll see from all along Mount’s Bay, just off the beach at Marazion. Up top there’s a castle with a priory church dating back to the 12th century; down below is a small harbour and village with cobbled lanes, shops and cafés.

Getting there is half the fun. At low tide a cobbled causeway appears and you can walk across in about 15 minutes; at high tide, little boats ferry people over from Marazion in the main season. The island only opens when the tide and weather allow, so check times before you set off and plan your day around them.

expect.title: Castle and summit
expect.text: It’s a steep, uneven climb up to the castle, but you’re rewarded with rooms full of stories and battlements looking right across Mount’s Bay. Guides give talks at the top.

expect.title: Terraced gardens
expect.text: Subtropical gardens cling to the cliffs in terraces. They’re only open in the warmer months, roughly May to early September.

expect.title: Harbour and village
expect.text: Pottering around the harbour is free in winter. There are shops, a café and the Steward’s House gallery, which shows Newlyn School paintings of everyday life in west Cornwall.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: Kids can follow the legendary giant’s footsteps up to the castle, and there are open lawns for little ones to run about on.

goodToKnow.label: Getting across
goodToKnow.text: Walk the causeway at low tide, or catch a boat at high tide between mid-March and the end of October. Only cross at the advised times: the tide comes in fast and the cobbles are uneven.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: In summer the island opens Sunday to Friday, with last entry at 3.45pm. Over winter the castle and gardens close, but you can still wander the harbour and village, browse the shops and gallery and visit the cafés for free when the causeway is open.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Castle and garden tickets are paid and cheaper booked ahead. Under-5s go free, there are family tickets, and National Trust members get a discount.

goodToKnow.label: Pushchairs and wheelchairs
goodToKnow.text: There’s no pushchair or wheelchair access up to the castle, and the causeway is hard work with wheels, so a baby carrier is easier. You can leave a pushchair opposite the shop.

goodToKnow.label: Weather
goodToKnow.text: Strong winds or rough seas can close the island, usually announced on the website and social media.

goodToKnow.label: Dogs
goodToKnow.text: Dogs are welcome in the village in the winter season.

week.text: Plan this one around the tide: the causeway is open for a few hours either side of low water. It pairs nicely with a beach morning in Mount’s Bay or an afternoon in Penzance, and it’s a good choice on a calm, settled day.

tips: Check the tide table before anything else and work backwards from it.
Wear trainers or boots: the causeway and the path to the castle are cobbled and slippery when wet.
Leave the pushchair behind and bring a baby carrier if you have little ones.
